extracted.intended_audience: NIAID/NIH grant reviewers and Makerere College of Health Sciences (MakCHS) research administrators / implementers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and implementing a project to strengthen institutional NIH/NIAID grants administration capacity at MakCHS through training of senior and junior administrators, a buddy mentorship program, an online community, SOP and systems improvement, and regional training outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award services
rubrics_metrics.description: Services the Grants Office provides before awards (Table 1): developing grants management standard operating procedures, policies and guidelines; finding relevant funding opportunities via Grants.gov and other sources; creating and maintaining institutional registrations on funding platforms like SAM.GOV, Grants.gov, eRA Commons; supporting proposal development including budgets and justifications, filling out proposal forms and institutional due diligence forms; timely submission of internally approved proposals and follow up on outcomes; conducting pre–award risk assessments for grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are core pre-award responsibilities to be offered by the Grants Office to ensure compliant and timely proposal submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award services
rubrics_metrics.description: Services the Grants Office provides after awards (Table 1): award negotiation and acceptance (reviewing terms and conditions, negotiating awards), award set up and orientation for project teams, safe custody of grant documents, project tracking and budget monitoring, compliance to grant regulations, preparing project amendments (budget modifications, carry overs), ensuring timely financial and programmatic reporting, facilitating audits, and successful project close out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-award functions intended to maintain compliance and timely reporting for NIH grants; these functions should be institutionalized in SOPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gap identification in current grants administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed limitations: majority of administrators have limited exposure to NIH policies and platforms (Grants.gov, eRA Commons, ASSIST), manual and error-prone tracking of expenditures and timelines, reliance on prime recipients for interpretation of funding rules (which may be misinterpreted), and insufficient institutional systems and guidelines to handle detailed NIH grant management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These identified gaps justify targeted capacity building activities; evaluation of project success should measure reduction of these gaps (e.g., improved platform use, reduced manual processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim 1 — Training two Senior Administrators (overall requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen capacity of two MakCHS Senior Administrators to efficiently and effectively manage NIH/NIAID grants through a combination of hands-on training at a US partner (GWU), in-house tailored training with NIAID's Grants Management Program (GMP), and attendance at the NIAID regional workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training forms and sequencing (GWU hands-on, NIAID GMP, regional workshop) are required; outcomes include transformation into Institutional Grants Management Leaders (IGML) who will mentor others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on training at Partner US Host Institution (GWU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four weeks of hands-on training at George Washington University (two weeks Year 1 + two weeks Year 2) with placements in appropriate research administration units; training schedule developed based on a prior training needs assessment and discussions with the GWU team leader; administrators under-study GWU systems and document lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress will be monitored twice weekly against set performance targets and timelines; debrief meetings after training to share lessons learnt and plan transfer of knowledge; prior sharing of training needs is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house tailored hands-on training with NIAID Grants Management Program (GMP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five-day tailored, hands-on training at NIAID GMP in Rockville, MD to augment GWU training, provide customized information on managing NIAID awards (financial management, grant tracking, Payment Management System, eRA Commons, Grants.gov) and offer clarification on NIH grants management rules and good business practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This training is complementary to GWU placement and should inform the senior administrators' plan to strengthen in-house practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance at NIAID regional workshop on program funding and grants administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in the NIAID regional workshop to fine-tune NIH grants management knowledge, enable interaction with NIAID scientific review officers and program officers, and provide networking opportunities with other regional research administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshop attendance is intended to provide 'insider scoop and tips' and to support institutional capacity via external networking and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring trainee progress and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: During GWU training progress will be monitored twice a week against set performance targets and timelines; a debrief meeting will be convened after each training to share lessons learned and achievements versus targets, and to plan knowledge transfer. Trainees will plan how to transfer knowledge and develop staff training and mentorship plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of regular monitoring, debriefs, and concrete transfer plans are required to demonstrate training effectiveness and to prepare trainees to serve as IGMLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award and Post-award training topics (training needs list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-award topics: acquiring NIH grants (finding opportunities, preparing/submitting applications), navigating NIH platforms (ASSIST, eRA Commons, Grants.gov, SAM), preparing proposal budgets and justifications, developing NIH Biosketches, writing Facilities & Resources page, identifying and managing Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI), assessing sub-awardees and due diligence. Post-award topics: navigating the Notice of Award, allowable/unallowable costs, NIH financial management policy, inventory and fixed asset management, level of effort reporting, preparing and submitting Federal Financial Reports, activities requiring prior approval, managing sub-contracts, monthly reconciliation of grant expenses, management of shared costs/matching, determination and appropriation of indirect costs, disposal and valuation of assets, no-cost and cost extensions, grant close out, procurement of project equipment, preparing for grant audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topic lists define the curriculum content to be delivered across trainings (senior, staff, investigator workshops, webinars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a staff training and mentorship plan (Aim 2a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a staff training and mentorship plan informed by lessons learned from GWU, NIAID GMP and regional workshop; the plan will guide preparation and delivery of training/mentorship and evolve into an in-house grants management professional development career track; engage module development experts to convert plan into a curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must be reviewed and approved by the Project Advisory Committee for fitness of use, financial sustainability and alignment with institutional strategic goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement staff training and mentorship plan (Aim 2b) — delivery modalities and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Training delivered as lunchtime didactic seminars to avoid disruption, with 69 administrators divided into groups by role (Grant Administrators, Accountants, Procurement officers, Human Resource Officers) receiving an average of four sessions over one month; facilitated by IGMLs and external specialists. Trainee progress monitored through weekly timesheets; participants may receive a certificate upon successful completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group-specific sessions, cross-participation where roles overlap, and use of weekly timesheets as monitoring data are required to demonstrate engagement and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Investigator short workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Short two-day workshops for 56 research investigators (two groups of 28) covering grant proposal writing and submission, budgeting and monitoring, grant reporting, cost/no-cost extensions and grant close out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops aim to educate investigators on NIH funding policies and the administrator role; targeting and scheduling (two groups of 28 for two days each) are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Administrator Buddy Program (RA-Buddy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pair junior research administrators with reliable, motivated, and knowledgeable Senior Administrators (buddies) to provide peer-to-peer support on finding funding, proposal preparation, navigating NIH platforms, budgeting, reporting and close out; buddies selected based on competency and willingness to mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance of the program monitored monthly by IGML using a short questionnaire completed by both junior and buddy; well-evaluated buddies recognized in the University newsletter and Annual Report; the system supports onboarding and continuous mentorship and is intended to run throughout and beyond the project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional webinars and external training outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Train 25 research administrators from other NIH recipient organizations in Uganda and East Africa via six webinars over three months; topics derived from training needs assessments; webinars include case studies, hands-on exercises, and Q&A, are recorded, and require prior registration and mailing-list communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Webinars reduce travel costs, increase reach, and recordings will be used for review and future training improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Learning Café (OLC) / Community of Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an online platform to keep administrators connected for real-time discussions and consultations on NIH policies, share SOPs, templates, checklists, training opportunities and other resources; archive discussions, include an online suggestion box, and use it to conduct training needs assessments and communicate upcoming trainings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Café is intended to transition into an online Community of Practice extending to external NIH grant recipients; recordings and archives serve as a repository for learning materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and improvement of grants management SOPs and guidelines (Aim 3a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review existing MakCHS grants management guidelines and SOPs to identify those requiring updates, and develop SOPs where none exist; consult researchers and PAC; developed and updated SOPs to be reviewed and approved by PAC and launched at a dissemination meeting; enforcement by grants administrators and investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAC approval and dissemination are required steps; successful implementation will contribute to better internal controls and increased compliance with NIAID/NIH funding rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen grants tracking and monitoring systems (Aim 3b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace manual Excel-based grant tracking with a Grant tracking Module integrated into existing Finance Management System (QuickBooks) to manage requisitions, payment approvals, automatic deadline reminders for PIs/accountants/administrators, and provide an online repository for all grant documents; selection of system based on flexibility and integration ability; system to be reviewed by PIT and approved by PAC prior to procurement; four grants administrators trained by system developers who then train others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System must improve real-time access, institutional memory, reduce errors, and be sustained by MakCHS overhead income; implementation requires PAC approval and staff training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability initiatives and institutionalization
rubrics_metrics.description: After project end, evolve the training and mentorship plan into an in-house grants management career track delivered quarterly through existing seminar series and online training (modest registration fee to meet facilitator costs); annual review/update of SOPs; integrate grants tracking into existing financial system to minimize maintenance costs; PAC to authorize and oversee sustainability and monitor quarterly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustainability depends on integration into institutional practices, modest fee recovery, PAC oversight, and quarterly monitoring and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project schedule, tasks and performance governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed project schedule over 18 months with kickoff meetings, development of workplan, setting targets & KPIs, monthly performance & progress review meetings by Implementation Team, quarterly PAC meetings, periodic webinars and trainings, business systems improvement plan development and implementation, evaluation activities, and project close-out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular governance meetings and KPI monitoring are required to track implementation; the schedule defines sequencing and responsible bodies (PIT, PAC, US Hosts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project management and administrative responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: PI (Stella Kakeeto) responsible for coordination, tracking milestones and monitoring impact; core team includes Co-Investigators (Grants and Contracts Manager, Finance Manager, Senior Grants Manager), supported by PAC and PIT; day-to-day administrative support by an administrative assistant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear assignment of responsibilities and support structures (PAC/PIT) is required for smooth implementation and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target participants and grouping for training
rubrics_metrics.description: Target 69 research administrators across four MakCHS schools (Biomedical Sciences 20, Public Health 18, Health Sciences 12, Medicine 19) grouped by function (Grant Administrators 24, Accountants 22, Procurement officers 5, Human Resource Officers 18) with specific, role-targeted training sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role-based grouping and scheduling (lunchtime seminars, average four sessions per group) to minimize disruption and tailor content; monitoring via timesheets.
